{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9 Version 2.jpg}}

#*To test if the cakes are done, insert a cake tester or skewer into the center. The tester should come out clean. If it doesn't, bake the cake for 3 to 5 more minutes and check again.<ref>https://www.thekitchn.com/5-ways-to-tell-when-your-cake-is-done-98927</ref>

#Cool the cakes and remove them from the pans. Take the cakes out of the oven and set them on a wire rack to cool. Once they're completely cooled down, turn them out and put them onto the wire rack.<ref>https://www.allnigerianrecipes.com/cakes/nigerian-cake/</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Stack and frost the cakes if you want a layer cake. Spread [[Make Buttercream Frosting|vanilla buttercream]] on 1 of the cakes and place the other cake on top. Spread more frosting on the top and sides.<ref>https://www.foodnetwork.com/how-to/articles/how-to-frost-a-cake-a-step-by-step-guide</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Bake the Nigerian cake in a preheated oven (300ºF) for 1 hour, or until the cake is springy to the touch.https://www.nigerianfoodtv.com/nigerian-cake-recipe-original-recipe/ Put both pans in the oven and bake them until they become golden brown and begin to pull away from the side of the pan.

{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9 Version 2.jpg}}
#*To test if the cakes are done, insert a cake tester or skewer into the center. The tester should come out clean. If it doesn't, bake the cake for 3 to 5 more minutes and check again.

#Cool the cakes and remove them from the pans. Take the cakes out of the oven and set them on a wire rack to cool. Once they're completely cooled down, turn them out and put them onto the wire rack.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Stack and frost the cakes if you want a layer cake. Spread [[Make Buttercream Frosting|vanilla buttercream]] on 1 of the cakes and place the other cake on top. Spread more frosting on the top and sides.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

added: #Preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F|C}} and grease 2 round pans. You can use two 8 or 9-in (20 or 23 cm) cake pans. Butter and flour the pans or spray them with baking spray.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 1 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Dissolve the powdered milk in the water. Measure 4 tablespoons (26 g) of powdered milk into a bowl and pour in {{convert|1/2|cup|ml}} of water. Whisk or stir until the powdered milk is completely dissolved.

{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 2.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 2-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 2 Version 2.jpg}}

#Whisk the flour, baking powder, and nutmeg together in a separate bowl. Put 4 cups (520 g) of plain flour into a large bowl and add 1 tablespoon (14 g) of baking powder. If you'd like the cake to be lightly spiced, add 1/2 teaspoon (1 g) of grated nutmeg.

{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 3.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 3-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 3 Version 2.jpg}}

#Cream the butter, margarine, and sugar for 5 to 10 minutes. Place 1 cup (226 g) of softened unsalted butter, 1 cup (226 g) of margarine, and 2 cups (400 g) of sugar into a large mixing bowl. Use an electric or stand mixer to beat them together on medium speed.

{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 4.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 4-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 4 Version 2.jpg}}

#Beat in 10 eggs 1 at a time on medium speed. Keep the mixer running while you add 1 egg at a time to the creamed mixture. Once the egg is incorporated, add the next egg. Continue beating them in until you've added a total of 10 eggs.

{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 5.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 5-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 5 Version 2.jpg}}

#Beat the batter for 2 minutes at medium-high speed and add the vanilla. Turn the mixer up and beat the batter so that it becomes pale. Then add {{convert|1|tbsp|ml}} of vanilla and beat it until it's incorporated.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 6 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Alternate adding the dry mixture and the milk. Turn the mixer to low and beat in about 1/3 of the dry mix. Then beat in half of the milk before you add another 1/3 of the dry mix. Beat in the rest of the milk and then the rest of the flour. Stop beating as soon as the last of the dry mix is incorporated.

{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 7.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 7-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 7 Version 2.jpg}}

#Divide the cake batter between the 2 prepared pans. Spoon half of the batter into 1 of the greased cake pans and spread the rest of the batter in the other cake pan. Use the back of the spoon to evenly spread the tops.

{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 8.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 8-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 8 Version 2.jpg}}

#Bake the Nigerian cake in a preheated oven (300ºF) for 1 hour, or until the cake is springy to the touch.https://www.nigerianfoodtv.com/nigerian-cake-recipe-original-recipe/ Put both pans in the oven and bake them until they become golden brown and begin to pull away from the side of the pan.

{{whvid|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9.360p.mp4|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9-preview.jpg|Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9 Version 2.jpg}}

#Cool the cakes and remove them from the pans. Take the cakes out of the oven and set them on a wire rack to cool. Once they're completely cooled down, turn them out and put them onto the wire rack.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 10 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Stack and frost the cakes if you want a layer cake. Spread [[Make Buttercream Frosting|vanilla buttercream]] on 1 of the cakes and place the other cake on top. Spread more frosting on the top and sides.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 11 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Serve the Nigerian cake. If you don't want to frost the cakes, you can sprinkle both cakes with sifted powdered sugar. Cut slices of cake and serve it along with soy milk, sugar cane juice, or kunnu aya.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 12 Version 2.jpg|center]]

#Alternate adding the dry mixture and the milk. Turn the mixer to low and beat in about 1/3 of the dry mix. Then beat in half of the milk before you add another 1/3 of the dry mix. #Bake the Nigerian cake in a preheated oven (300ºF) for 1 hour, or until the cake is springy to the touch.<ref>https://www.nigerianfoodtv.com/nigerian-cake-recipe-original-recipe/</ref> Put both pans in the oven and bake them until they become golden brown and begin to pull away from the side of the pan.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9.jpg|center]]

#Stack and frost the cakes if you want a layer cake. Spread [[Make Buttercream Frosting|vanilla buttercream]] on 1 of the cakes and place the other cake on top. Spread more frosting on the top and sides.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 11.jpg|center]]

#Serve the Nigerian cake. If you don't want to frost the cakes, you can sprinkle both cakes with sifted powdered sugar. Cut slices of cake and serve it along with soy milk, sugar cane juice, or kunnu aya.[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 12.jpg|center]]

#Cream the butter, margarine, and sugar for 5 to 10 minutes. Place 1 cup (226 g) of softened unsalted butter, 1 cup (226 g) of margarine, and 2 cups (400 g) of sugar into a large mixing bowl. Use an electric or stand mixer to beat them together on medium speed.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 4.jpg|center]]

#Beat in 10 eggs 1 at a time on medium speed. Keep the mixer running while you add 1 egg at a time to the creamed mixture. Once the egg is incorporated, add the next egg. Continue beating them in until you've added a total of 10 eggs.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 5.jpg|center]]

#Beat the batter for 2 minutes at medium-high speed and add the vanilla. Turn the mixer up and beat the batter so that it becomes pale. Then add {{convert|1|tbsp|ml}} of vanilla and beat it until it's incorporated.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 6.jpg|center]]

#Alternate adding the dry mixture and the milk. Turn the mixer to low and beat in about 1/3 of the dry mix. Then beat in half of the milk before you add another 1/3 of the dry mix. Beat in the rest of the milk and then the rest of the flour. Stop beating as soon as the last of the dry mix is incorporated.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 7.jpg|center]]

#Divide the cake batter between the 2 prepared pans. Spoon half of the batter into 1 of the greased cake pans and spread the rest of the batter in the other cake pan. Use the back of the spoon to evenly spread the tops.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 8.jpg|center]]

#Bake the Nigerian cake for 45 to 55 minutes. Put both pans in the oven and bake them until they become golden brown and begin to pull away from the side of the pan.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 9.jpg|center]]

#Cool the cakes and remove them from the pans. Take the cakes out of the oven and set them on a wire rack to cool. Once they're completely cooled down, turn them out and put them onto the wire rack.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 10.jpg|center]]

#Stack and frost the cakes if you want a layer cake. Spread [[Make Buttercream Frosting|vanilla buttercream]] on 1 of the cakes and place the other cake on top. Spread more frosting on the top and sides.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 11.jpg|center]]

#Serve the Nigerian cake. If you don't want to frost the cakes, you can sprinkle both cakes with sifted powdered sugar. Cut slices of cake and serve it along with soy milk, sugar cane juice, or kunnu aya.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>[[Image:Bake Nigerian Cake Step 12.jpg|center]]

added: [[Category:Cakes]]
[[Category:Baking]]

If you're looking for a rich cake that's easy to mix, make Nigerian cake. Cream butter and margarine with sugar until it's fluffy. Then beat in flour with baking powder along with milk. Spread the batter in 2 round pans and bake the cakes until they're golden brown. Nigerian cake is great when served simply, but you can frost and stack the cakes or cover them with fondant.
==Ingredients==
*4 cups (520 g) all-purpose flour
*2 cups (400 g) sugar
*1 cup (226 g) unsalted butter, softened
*1 cup (226 g) margarine
*10 eggs at room temperature
*{{convert|1|tbsp|ml}} vanilla
*4 tablespoons (26 g) powdered milk '''or''' {{convert|1/2|cup|ml}} milk
*{{convert|1/2|cup|ml}} water, if using powdered milk
*1 tablespoon (14 g) baking powder
*1/2 teaspoon (1 g) grated nutmeg, optional
''Makes 2 round 8 or 9-in (20 or 23 cm) cakes''
==Steps==
===Mixing the Batter===

#Preheat the oven to {{convert|350|F|C}} and grease 2 round pans. You can use two 8 or 9-in (20 or 23 cm) cake pans. Butter and flour the pans or spray them with baking spray.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>
#*To make it even easier to remove the cakes, consider lining the pans with parchment paper.

#Dissolve the powdered milk in the water. Measure 4 tablespoons (26 g) of powdered milk into a bowl and pour in {{convert|1/2|cup|ml}} of water. Whisk or stir until the powdered milk is completely dissolved.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>
#*If you prefer, use {{convert|1/2|cup|ml}} of liquid milk instead of reconstituting the powdered milk.

#Whisk the flour, baking powder, and nutmeg. Put 4 cups (520 g) of all-purpose flour into a large bowl and add 1 tablespoon (14 g) of baking powder. If you'd like the cake to be lightly spiced, add 1/2 teaspoon (1 g) of grated nutmeg.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>
#*Whisk the dry ingredients for about 30 seconds so they're combined.

#Cream the butter, margarine, and sugar for 5 to 10 minutes. Place 1 cup (226 g) of softened unsalted butter, 1 cup (226 g) of margarine, and 2 cups (400 g) of sugar into a large mixing bowl. Use an electric or stand mixer to beat them on medium speed.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>
#*The creamed mixture should become pale and fluffy.
#*If you don't have a mixer, use a wooden spoon. Keep in mind that it will take 5 to 10 minutes longer to cream the mixture by hand.

#Beat in 10 eggs 1 at a time on medium speed. Keep the mixer running while you add 1 egg at a time to the creamed mixture. Once the egg is incorporated, add the next egg. Continue beating them in until you've added a total of 10 eggs.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>
#*Room temperature eggs will blend into the batter the best. If they're cold the batter may separate, but it will come together again when you add the dry ingredients.

#Beat the batter for 2 minutes at medium-high and add the vanilla. Turn the mixer up and beat the batter so it becomes pale. Then add {{convert|1|tbsp|ml}} of vanilla and beat it until it's incorporated.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>

#Alternate adding the dry mixture and the milk. Turn the mixer to low and beat in about 1/3 of the dry mix. Then beat in half of the milk before you add another 1/3 of the dry mix. Beat in the rest of the milk and then the rest of the flour. Stop beating as soon as the last of the dry mix is incorporated.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>
#*It's fine if there are a few lumps in the cake batter.
#*Overbeating the batter will make the cake tough and dense.
===Baking the Cakes===

#Divide the cake batter between the 2 prepared pans. Spoon half of the batter into 1 of the greased cake pans and spread the rest of the batter in the other cake pan. Use the back of the spoon to evenly spread the tops.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>

#Bake the Nigerian cake for 45 to 55 minutes. Put both pans in the oven and bake them until they become golden brown and begin to pull away from the side of the pan.<ref>http://www.gratednutmeg.com/?p=4376</ref>
#*To test if the cakes are done, insert a cake tester or skewer into the center. The tester should come out clean. If it doesn't, bake the cake for 3 to 5 more minutes and check again.
#Cool the cakes completely and remove them from the pans. Take the cakes out of the oven and set them on a wire rack to cool. Once they're totally cool, turn them out onto the wire rack.

#Serve the Nigerian cake. While you don't need to frost or coat the cakes, you can sprinkle both cakes with sifted powdered sugar. Cut slices of cake and serve it along with soy milk, sugar cane juice, or kunnu aya.

#*If you'd like to stack the cakes to make 1 layer cake, spread [[Make Buttercream Frosting|vanilla buttercream]] on the layers. You can also [[Fondant a Cake|spread rolled fondant]] on the top for an extra special look.
#*Cover and store leftover cake in an airtight container at room temperature for 1 to 2 days or in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
==Tips==
*If you'd like to include brandy for flavor, beat 1 to 2 tablespoons (15 to 30 ml) into the batter when you add the vanilla.
==Things You'll Need==
*Measuring cups and spoons
*Bowls
*Spoons
*Electric mixer with beater attachment
*Baking spray
*Parchment paper, optional
*Cake tester or skewer
*2 round 8 or 9-in (20 or 23 cm) cake pans
*Wire racks
